stem: Following is NOT a part of Tetralogy of Fallot:
explanation: Tetralogy of Fallot comprises VSD, overriding aorta, right ventricular outflow (pulmonary) stenosis and right ventricular hypertrophy; ASD is not part of it (adding an ASD makes the pentalogy of Fallot).

stem: A 14-year-old boy is seen by a paediatric cardiologist because of increasing shortness of breath. Studies reveal increased pulmonary vascular resistance, left axis deviation on ECG, and a mitral regurgitation murmur. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: An ostium primum ASD (partial AV septal defect) has a cleft anterior mitral leaflet causing mitral regurgitation and characteristically left axis deviation, and often presents later in childhood. Secundum defects cause right axis deviation, and a complete AV canal usually presents with heart failure in infancy.
key_note: Bank marked E; correct is A because survival to 14 with left axis deviation and mitral regurgitation fits an ostium primum (partial AV canal) defect; complete AV canal presents in infancy.

stem: Which of the following is a cause of Eisenmenger syndrome?
explanation: Eisenmenger syndrome is reversal of a left to right shunt (VSD, ASD, PDA) once pulmonary vascular resistance exceeds systemic, causing cyanosis. VSD is the commonest cause.
